Footpad impact test on RS soil (Red Crushed Volcanic Scoria (narrowly graded)) at relative density 0.65; apparatus: subscale oblique impact test equipment; loading: vertical impact; moving weight not printed. Recorded: vertical force vs time; displacement vs time; vertical force vs displacement. One of 2 tests drawn from the same figures.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The numbers below were digitized from the published figure by two readings made separately; they agree within the stated reading bounds at 144 of the 198 points, and 17 are still under review. They have not yet been checked by a person. The test setup is incomplete: fill depth, moving mass are not reported.
:::

## Data

![vertical force against time; displacement against time; vertical force against displacement, SI units, this test in red and the other tests printed in Fig. 4-19 in gray. Error bars are reading bounds (half-widths from the digitization), not standard deviations. Filled markers were agreed by both readings, hollow ones were not.](../img/plots/b68-imp-12.png){.lightbox}

Peak vertical force 2616 N at 4.29 ms time; 118.2 N at 130 ms, the end of the record. Displacement 31.35 mm at the end.

Download: [observations.csv](../files/data/experiments/b68-imp-12/observations.csv) (198 points: 0 plotted symbols, 180 samples of the drawn curve; columns `x_si`, `y_si` with bounds `x_bound_si`, `y_bound_si`; panel 1 (Fig. 4-19): vertical force in N against time in s; panel 2 (Fig. 4-19): displacement in m against time in s; panel 3 (Fig. 4-20): vertical force in N against displacement in m; the printed-unit values, the pixel position on the scan and the review status of each point are kept in further columns) and [series.json](../files/data/experiments/b68-imp-12/series.json) (units, conversion factors, how the points were read).

Reading bounds on these figures (how far our reading of the printed figure may be off, not the uncertainty of the test): typical bound 0.789 ms in time, typical bound 333 micrometers in displacement, 17.4 N in vertical force (Fig. 4-19) (0.7 percent of the peak), 669 micrometers in displacement (Fig. 4-19), 15.16 N in vertical force (Fig. 4-20). Both independent readings agree within these bounds at 144 of the 198 points; 17 are still under review (hollow in the plot) and 37 were settled against the scan. Check the digitized points against the scan: [F4-19](../figures/index.qmd#check-f4-19), [F4-20](../figures/index.qmd#check-f4-20).

**About these values.** Past 100 ms the printed time labels skip 110: the evenly spaced lines after the 100 ms line are labeled 120, 130 and 140 and the frame after them is unlabeled. The values read those lines as 110, 120 and 130 ms and the frame as 140 ms, from the even spacing. Taken as printed, a time between the 100 ms line and the next would be up to 10 ms later (the difference grows across that interval) and every later time 10 ms later. Fig. 4-20 cannot test this: the same rescaling of both time axes leaves force against displacement unchanged. Fig. 4-20 plots the force of panel 1 against the displacement of panel 2: the same runs, cross-plotted from the same records.
